method: We compared the zero-ozone ENERGY STAR certified air purifiers with the highest certified smoke CADR. Smoke CADR carries 85% of the weight and the five-year electricity cost 15% (cost is scored against the page's cheapest unit, so a larger share would let a slow but cheap unit lead), computed from the certified yearly energy use and the current EIA U.S. average residential price. Rated room size is left out of the score because ENERGY STAR derives it from smoke CADR.
name: Best air purifiers for smoke, ranked mainly by certified smoke CADR
scoring: each value scored against the best on the page (best = 1), times its weight; total out of 100

excluded.why: conservative choice: only units that report 0 ppb ozone in certification; UL's zero-ozone test (UL 2998) cannot quantify low readings, so this also drops units whose small non-zero reports are not reliably different from 0

excluded.filter: certified yearly energy far from what its own smoke CADR and CADR per watt imply
excluded.why: yearly energy, smoke CADR and CADR per watt are linked on almost every record of this list; where they disagree this much the record contradicts itself, so neither its running cost nor its efficiency can be trusted. The one dropped here is the CleanAirKits Luggable Ultra (5-fan) (certified as Rainbow Luggable Ultra, record 4518200), whose smoke CADR is below this list's cut anyway
